Vanessa / Neha — technical inputs below that I think will map into the CAIQ/LLM tabs. Opening notes: I'm putting conservative, evidence-backed statements only. If legal wants stronger language we'll need approval for changes.

1) Training on customer prompts/responses:
- Default hosted API behavior: we do NOT use customer prompts/responses to train or improve Redwood's base models. We may use de-identified telemetry (service-level metrics) for platform health and performance only.
- Opt-in data use: Customers may elect to allow model improvement by explicit contract addendum and secure ingestion pipeline; this is not enabled by default.

2) Retention windows (default):
- Hosted API: transient transcripts are persisted for 30 days to support debugging, abuse detection, billing dispute investigations, and quality monitoring. After 30 days we run automated deletion jobs; deletion is reflected in audit logs with object lifecycle events.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): configurable by contract; typical default configured retention is 0-7 days unless the customer requests otherwise.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): persistence is customer-controlled; Redwood does not access on-prem data unless explicitly configured by customer-hosted agents.

3) Storage & encryption:
- Stored in encrypted S3 buckets (us-west-2) for hosted API. Objects are encrypted at rest with AES-256; server-side encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS is supported for enterprise customers (Dedicated/Private recommended).
- Access to transcripts is limited by IAM roles and audited. We maintain object-level lifecycle policies for deletion and CloudTrail events for access.

4) Evidence artifacts we can provide quickly:
- IAAS: CloudTrail bucket access logs & lifecycle event samples (redacted).
- KMS integration guide & audit snapshot showing CMK bindings.
- Example delete-job run output (timestamped).
- Draft "No-Train" attestation (I attached a proposal PDF).

5) Caveat on logs and artefacts: we must redact customer PII in any shared logs. Production audit exports can be scheduled and will require a data sharing agreement.

I attached the draft attestation and I've started populating the CAIQ spreadsheet. Happy to jump on a quick call with Amanda if they want details.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_no_train_attestation.pdf (pdf)

Amanda — thanks for the clear asks and timeline. Please find attached: (1) our completed CAIQ answers (tabbed to the LLM questions), (2) a short "No-Train" attestation signed by our Head of Security, and (3) a 1-page DPIA summary focused on transcript handling and HIPAA considerations.

High-level summary we provided to your team:
- Redwood does NOT use customer prompts/responses to improve our base models by default. Any model training using customer data is only performed if the customer explicitly signs an opt-in contract addendum and routes data through our secure ingestion pipeline.
- Default hosted retention window for request/response transcripts is 30 days; after 30 days transcripts are deleted via automated lifecycle policies and deletion events are logged in CloudTrail. We documented the S3 bucket encryption scheme and availability of CMK (customer-managed keys) for enterprise customers.
- Dedicated instances are configurable and can be set to minimal retention (0-7 days) or fully disabled depending on contract. Private deployments are under customer control and Redwood has no access unless expressly configured.

Attachments included: redwood_partial_caiq_answers.xlsx (completed LLM tabs), redwood_no_train_attestation.pdf (signed), DPIA_onepager_redwood_sundance.pdf.

Next steps: if Sundance security team wants sample redacted CloudTrail event exports or a short walkthrough of KMS bindings, Karthik can join a 30-minute call. Can you propose times on Feb 18-19 PT?

Best,
